data.title: FOREX-Euro sinks on French debt worries, yen gains for week on AI rout
data.description:
(Updated in New York afternoon time)

* Euro drops on concerns over French unrest, Moody's rating decision awaited

* Japanese yen benefits from safe-haven flow after AI rout

* US dollar index to end week little changed

By Karen Brettell

Oct 23 (Reuters) - The euro fell on Friday and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen as a selloff in French government bonds pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.

The Japanese yen was headed for a weekly increase against the greenback as it benefited from safe-haven flows from the selloff in AI stocks on Thursday. The dollar index was little changed on the week.

The euro was hit by concerns about growing unrest in France and the country's worsening budget problems. France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country also faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody's on Friday.

"The pressure in the European bond market has eased today, but Moody's review of France's debt rating late today poses a challenge, and although the Macron government has threatened military assistance to quell the social unrest, more activity is likely this weekend," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex.

The euro was last down 0.21% at $1.1191, set to end the week 0.43% lower. It fell more sharply against the yen, touching its lowest level since October 2025 at 175.08 yen . It was last down 0.11% against the Japanese currency and on track for a weekly decline of 1.1%.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.25% to 101.82 and was headed for a weekly gain of 0.03%.

The yen weakened 0.1% to 156.9 per dollar and was on track for a weekly gain of around 0.7%, its best week since mid-September.

"The yen has continued to trade at stronger levels at the end of this week, encouraged by more risk-off trading conditions," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

CENTRAL BANK POLICY MEETINGS IN FOCUS

Traders are looking to next week's policy meetings at the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan. All three are expected to leave rates unchanged, but investors will look for clues on the future path of policy.

Fed funds futures traders trimmed bets on a December hike after Thursday's stock market selloff, though they still see an 81% chance of such a move, according to LSEG data.

Traders see a 66% chance of an ECB hike in December. Investors will scrutinize any hint of the rate outlook after ECB President Christine Lagarde said in late September that a moderate policy response to inflation was appropriate.

Purchasing Managers' Index data showed private-sector growth in the euro zone slowed in October to its weakest pace in four months, hurt by a renewed contraction in France.

"The drop brings the PMIs back in line with other growth indicators, in our view, rather than suggesting downside risks from here," Giada Giani, an economist at Citi, said. "France remains a drag, but the rest of the euro area remains resilient."

In Japan, data on Friday showed annual core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2% target in September for the first time in nine months. The reading points to broadening price pressures and strengthens the case for a near-term rate hike, analysts said.

Traders are pricing in 61% odds of a BOJ hike in December.

(Reporting by Karen Brettell; Additional reporting by Stefano Rebaudo; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria and Rod Nickel)

data.title: Democrat on US FCC urges broadcast industry to be more aggressive confronting the agency
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - The sole Democratic member of the Federal Communications Commission on Friday urged the broadcast industry to take a more aggressive approach in confronting the Trump administration's actions toward major US networks and stations.

FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez called on the National Association of Broadcasters to address the administration's efforts to challenge broadcasters on a series of fronts, including a warning from FCC Chair Brendan Carr that US broadcast networks could violate their regulatory obligations by airing "entirely fake polls" before the November 3 election.

"This administration is running a coordinated, government-wide effort to reshape the media into its sanctioned messenger," Gomez warned, adding that Carr was seeking to pressure networks into not running polls the administration dislikes, which she said was not proper.

Carr, who has repeatedly faced pressure from President Donald Trump to crack down on ⁠US broadcasters and journalists, in April ordered an unprecedented early license review for all eight of Disney's ( DIS ) company-owned ABC TV stations.

A spokesperson for Carr did not immediately comment.

NAB President Curtis LeGeyt said in a statement that the group appreciated Gomez's "recognition of the value of local broadcasters and her commitment to the First Amendment principles that underpin a free press."

"We will continue working with her and all policymakers to protect broadcasters' rights," he said.

Gomez said the NAB had been "largely quiet through the first year of this censorship and control campaign" but that it had not stayed "completely silent."

An "industry confronting a coordinated effort to turn licensing authority into leverage over election-year coverage needs more than a couple of tempered statements," she added.

In April, the NAB said the Disney ( DIS ) early-renewal decision "creates ‌significant uncertainty for all broadcasters" and argued the "FCC must be careful to avoid actions that create further instability for the local stations viewers and listeners depend on."

The FCC also said earlier this ⁠year that ​late-night and daytime talk shows are no longer bona fide news programs ​that are exempt from equal-time rules for interviews with political candidates.

(Reporting by David Shepardson Editing by Bill Berkrot)

data.title: Chili's workers' lawsuit looks to strike New York state's lower wage for tipped workers
data.description:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - A lawsuit filed on Friday involving the pay practices of Chili's ( EAT ) operator Brinker International ( EAT ) is seeking to strike down New York state's lower minimum wage for workers who earn tips, which it claims fuels the sexual and racial harassment of workers.

The proposed class action in federal court in Brooklyn by three former Chili's employees claims that New York's policy, which most other US states share, allows Brinker ( EAT ) to force employees to rely on tips and exposes them to unlawful discrimination.

"Brinker ( EAT ) promotes a culture in which tipped service employees make customers 'feel special,' even at the expense of their dignity and safety," the lawsuit says.

Brinker ( EAT ) did not respond to a request for comment. The New York Attorney General's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the challenge to the state law. 

Many worker advocates have for years called for the elimination of sub-minimum wages that companies may pay to workers who earn tips under federal and most state laws, as long as tips make up the difference. 

In New York, where the minimum wage is $16 an hour or $17 in and around New York City, food service workers who earn tips may be paid $10.70 or $11.35 an hour. The federal tipped minimum wage is $2.13 an hour, compared with the traditional minimum wage of $7.25, and applies in states that do not set their own minimums.

RELYING ON TIPS

Advocates say that because tips are discretionary and unpredictable, they should supplement workers' incomes rather than make up most of their pay. The lawsuit against Brinker ( EAT ) says that relying on tips forces workers to tolerate conduct such as sexual harassment and customers' potential racial bias.

The plaintiffs' lawyers said in the lawsuit that they plan to expand the case to include a nationwide class of Chili's ( EAT ) workers.

Brinker ( EAT ) operates more than 1,200 Chili's ( EAT ) restaurants in the US, including 36 in New York. The company also owns Maggiano's Little Italy ( EAT ), an Italian restaurant chain with about 50 US locations.

The lawsuit claims that Chili's ( EAT ) reliance on customer ratings to determine workers' schedules, shifts and table assignments is also unlawful. The ratings system can be racially biased, the lawsuit says, and can make it difficult for servers to reject unwanted advances from customers for fear of a poor rating.

The named plaintiffs, three former employees at a Chili's ( EAT ) in the Glendale section of Queens in New York City, claim they were routinely subjected to sexual advances and inappropriate comments and that management did not adequately protect workers from harassment.

(Reporting by Daniel Wiessner in Albany, New York, Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi and Rod Nickel)

data.title: US to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods to help Republicans in midterms, WSJ reports
data.description:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - The United States is expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a bid to help Maine Senator Susan Collins and other Republicans from northern US states in the upcoming midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar.

The reductions could be balanced out by raising levies on other Canadian goods, the report said, adding that a proclamation altering the tariffs could come as early as Friday.

A White House official told the Journal that any tariff announcements would come directly from the administration and that any preliminary reporting is speculation. The White House didn't immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Senator Collins, in a statement issued shortly after the WSJ report, said that nine categories of products, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers, will be exempted from U.S. tariffs on Canada.

The Commerce Department did not immediately provide a comment on her announcement, which comes as she is trying to win a sixth term to the senate in Democratic-leaning Maine.

Republican candidates in ​northern US border states most affected by the tariffs are trying to strike a balance between appealing to Trump's loyal base and winning independent voters.

The economies of Michigan and Maine have long been intertwined with Canada's, covering everything from auto parts to lumber to fruit-picking equipment. That has raised the stakes in two states that Republicans will likely need to win in the November 3 elections if they are to hold the US Senate.

US President Donald Trump ​said on Friday that Canada is ‌working on a trade deal with the United States, though the two nations ​have been locked in a ​standoff since talks broke down in August, triggering new ‌tariffs ⁠and retaliation on both sides of the border.

(Reporting by Kanjyik Ghosh in Barcelona;)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

data.title: Senator says planned Meta commercial terms update could harm US businesses
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' ( META ) plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators.

Blackburn, who is chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, said the updated terms "indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses by granting itself sweeping authority to scrape content from any website associated with Facebook and Instagram business accounts." 

Earlier on Friday, Meta said it would delay the implementation of updated commercial terms from October 30 until November 20, so it can address concerns ​from publishers and digital advertisers.

EU and UK antitrust authorities have received complaints about the new commercial terms, which publishers and digital advertisers said would give Meta unlimited rights to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims.

Blackburn said that Meta previously revised its terms to remove an explicit reference to AI training but said the changes did not go far enough. She added that the revised language authorizes extensive scraping of external websites and permits Meta to "develop" its business products with collected content.

"Without clear restrictions on how that information may be used, including whether it may be incorporated into AI systems, Meta's revisions offer little assurance that creators' intellectual property will be protected," Blackburn said. She added: "This is particularly troubling for American news publishers, creators, and small businesses that rely on Meta's platforms to reach their audiences and customers."

Asked for comment on Blackburn's letter, Meta on Friday noted it had delayed the change and said the revised terms apply only to its ads and business products and that it is not changing how it uses web crawlers.

"These updates don't give us new rights to supersede such preferences and this isn't about scraping news sites," the company said, noting that "content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences."

Publishers worldwide are ramping up fights with AI companies using their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair-use arguments.

"Meta must withdraw the updated Commercial Terms and come to the table to protect the content of creators and publishers across the country," Blackburn said. "American creators and small businesses are not a free source of content for Meta to exploit."

(Reporting by David Shepardson in Washington; Editing by Nick Zieminski and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
data.description:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy on the doorstep of midterm congressional elections centering on affordability issues, a survey showed on Friday.

The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 46.3, which had also been the index's preliminary reading for October.

October's reading marked the second-lowest on record after the all-time low of 44.8 set in May, not long after the Iran war began.

"Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."

The survey results dovetail with political polling data showing voters have a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's stewardship over it.

Millions of US voters have already cast early ballots in the fast-approaching November 3 midterm election that will determine control of Congress over the final two years of Trump's term. Polls show Republicans are likely to lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate as Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll sits at a record low thanks to the skyrocketing fuel prices unleashed by his decision to attack Iran in late February.

University of Michigan data broken down by political party affiliation showed the weaker sentiment was led by survey respondents self-identified as independents, who comprise a critical bloc of swing voters. Their sentiment score dropped to 42.4 - just above May's record-low 40.6 - from 47.7 in September, while scores for Democrats and Republicans improved.

The survey showed a significant upswing this year among independents - and also notably Republicans - citing high prices as a drag on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents referencing inflation pressures as hurting their financial situation rose by 27%, while it has shot up by 52% among Republicans. Similar citations among Democrats, meanwhile, are up by 15%.

Households with no or limited exposure to the stock market - until recently climbing rapidly on enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence investment boom - also have cited high prices as a drag on their finances more frequently than at the start of the year.

STICKY INFLATION EXPECTATIONS

The survey's measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the next year nudged up to 4.7% from 4.6% in September. Twelve-month inflation expectations have surged from 3.4% in February before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.

Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years rose to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, just after the war's start.

Hsu, in an accompanying report on inflation expectations released with the October sentiment survey, said the persistence of elevated inflation expectations in the post-COVID-19 pandemic era posed a risk for Federal Reserve policymakers' efforts to return inflation to their 2% target - unachieved now for more than five years.

"Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year's increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu wrote. "The fact that aggregate consumer spending has been relatively resilient despite negative views of the economy provides another reason for caution. If part of consumption currently reflects precautionary spending to avoid future price hikes, disinflation may be even more difficult to achieve."

Fed officials meet next week in Washington, and despite recent higher-than-expected inflation readings in the last two weeks they are broadly expected to leave their policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00% after raising it by a quarter percentage point in September. Most Fed officials have indicated they see a need for higher rates, but key leaders also have expressed a willingness to wait for more data before their next move.

(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: FCC grants Intel waiver to use existing foreign-made robotic devices
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it has granted a waiver to Intel ( INTC ) from its ban on some foreign-made advanced robotics to allow it to continue to use some vehicles critical to semiconductor production.

The FCC said it would grant a one-year waiver of its rules in order to prevent "potential disruptions in the availability of domestic semiconductor manufacturing services for Intel's ( INTC ) customers."

Intel ( INTC ) in a petition last week said the robotic devices are critical to its US semiconductor manufacturing. Without the waiver, Intel ( INTC ) would not have been allowed to make software, firmware, and hardware changes for its "Automated Guided Vehicles" that it said could be classified by the agency as robots.

Intel ( INTC ) told the FCC there is a lack of proven domestic alternatives that meet operational requirements and replacing the automated guided vehicles would take Intel ( INTC ) years and could disrupt its manufacturing operations.

An FCC official said the waiver would allow Intel ( INTC ) to make minor changes to existing models of vehicles and does not involve swapping out any US-made components for foreign-made components.

Intel ( INTC ) said it appreciated the approval of its petition that "supports American manufacturing of leading-edge chips."

The vehicles are used to transport materials within Intel's ( INTC ) semiconductor facilities and have been in operation for over two decades, the company said.

In July, the FCC barred imports of new Chinese robots and power inverters, seeking to protect the US AI buildout from national ​security threats and reshore key industries slated for explosive growth.

The FCC barred imports of new Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots, ‌in addition to connected power inverters. The FCC has since granted some approvals to allow for continued specific robotic device imports.

Some analysts forecast broad adoption of humanoid robots, topped with AI-enabled "brains," ​in consumer and industrial arenas, while explosive data-center construction in the US will depend on reliable sources of inverters.

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chris Reese and Bill Berkrot)

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

Oct 23 (Reuters) - The tech-heavy Nasdaq edged higher on Friday, helped by signs of stabilization in some tech stocks, while telecom shares tumbled on concerns that SpaceX's entry in the sector could heighten competition and threaten their market share.

For the week, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were on track for losses, while the blue-chip Dow remained slightly higher, supported by gains in defensive stocks.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 1.4%, as some chip-related stocks gained on Friday. Nvidia ( NVDA ) was up 0.3%, while Micron Technology ( MU ) and Intel ( INTC ) gained 2.5% and 3.8%, respectively.

AI-related shares swung sharply this month, first coming under pressure over CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) debt burden and the cost of financing AI investment.

On Thursday, the Nasdaq fell again, logging the biggest single-day drop in four months. The slide accelerated following Meta's nearly 8% decline after the company reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade amid concerns over its AI-related expenditures.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares were down 2.3% on Friday.

"Investors are still trying to wrap their heads around the sheer size of this AI spend. The sheer size of these notional dollars is staggering, but we aren't at the point of the cycle yet that we've seen this return," said James O'Day, head of equities at Citizens Bank.

"The market's probably healthier than it feels."

The S&P 500 communication services index was down 0.6%, as AT&T ( T ), Verizon and T-Mobile fell between 1.3% and 5.6% after a report said SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a nationwide wireless carrier program. SpaceX shares gained 2.2%.

US cell tower operators gained from this news, with Crown Castle ( CCI ) up 11.11% and American Tower ( AMT ) up 4.8%.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with major companies such as Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet and Amazon ( AMZN ) reporting next week.

data.title: Apple's foldable iPhone hits stores with $2,000 price tag and scarce supply
data.description:
By Aditya Soni, Christine Chen and Will Russell

SYDNEY/SHANGHAI/LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Apple's ( AAPL ) first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, hit stores around the world on Friday with a price tag of about $2,000 and less of the fanfare that accompanied previous iPhone launches.

From Singapore and Shanghai to London and San Francisco, demand was strong but with sales rationed, there were fewer of the round-the-block queues and overnight camp-outs that once marked new iPhone days.

Competitors such as Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) and Huawei Technologies have sold premium foldable phones for years and the Duo is a test of whether Apple ( AAPL ) can reinvent the small foldable mobile market the way the iPhone did for smartphones.

It is also an early challenge for Apple's ( AAPL ) new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September.

Apple's ( AAPL ) estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January within minutes of pre-orders opening a week ago, as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response "nothing short of extraordinary".

Apple ( AAPL ) capped pre-orders at two handsets per customer and limited sales to walk-in shoppers. In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan they were only available to those who had ordered online.

In Sydney, where the first Apple ( AAPL ) store began selling the new passport-shaped phones on Friday, a queue formed outside before opening at 8 a.m. local time (2100 GMT).

"This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it's so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life's too short," said Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer who paid A$3,899 ($2,734) for a 512GB Duo.

CEO Ternus played greeter at a store in Austin, Texas, throwing open the doors and high-fiving customers as they streamed in, a video posted on X by CBS Austin showed.

A known car enthusiast, Ternus's Austin visit coincides with this weekend's Formula 1 US Grand Prix in the city, with Apple ( AAPL ) holding exclusive US broadcast and streaming rights to the racing series.

At Apple's ( AAPL ) Fifth Avenue store in New York, marketing head Greg Joswiak opened the doors to a crowd of customers, social media posts showed. Some posts said people had camped outside the store since as early as 4 a.m. local time (0800 GMT).

Mohit Chandel, a 32-year-old San Francisco resident and consultant, had promised his father in Singapore an iPhone Duo for his retirement but forgot to pre-order one.

So when he spotted a dozen people lining up outside an Apple ( AAPL ) store around 11 p.m. Thursday, he joined them, ordered a bench and pillow from Walgreens and settled in for the night.

"He doesn't know that. All the pre-orders are gone. He's expecting a Duo sometime in the mail so now I have to buy it," Chandel said.

In China, a soft consumer market and rising memory costs have led to six straight quarters of declining smartphone shipments, although Apple's ( AAPL ) market share has rebounded as some buyers trade up to premium devices.

Liu Wei, a 26-year-old healthcare professional, already has a foldable phone from Xiaomi, but still queued outside a Shanghai store from 6 a.m. for Apple's ( AAPL ) first foldable.

"I've used Apple ( AAPL ) products for many years and I have more trust (in the brand), so I bought one on launch day to try it out," he said.

Many queued to pick up pre-orders, while others hoped for limited stock or to browse display models.

Others were resellers.

In Hong Kong, May, 38, who declined to give his full name, bought a 256GB iPhone Duo, priced at HK$17,499 ($2,231.73), in an online pre-sale and planned to resell it for a profit of around HK$4,000. "A few meals' worth of money," he joked.

Paul Francis, 53, was one of several dozen fans who queued overnight outside London's Regent Street store in pouring rain.

"Some people think it was mad. Including myself," the charity manager said.

MIXED REVIEWS

Early reviews have praised the Duo's design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers.

But reviewers said camera compromises, including no telephoto lens, and third-party apps still to be reworked for the new display size could disappoint some buyers.

They also said the folded Duo is less handy for the quick tasks most users do daily and several prominent reviewers recommended against it for many Apple ( AAPL ) customers.

"It's been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I've gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype - not a finished product that I'd want to buy and carry," wrote longtime Apple ( AAPL ) commentator John Gruber.

Tech commentator Marques Brownlee said in a YouTube review that for a regular person who mostly texts and browses, "it is probably a no. But if the $2,000 doesn't mean much to you, and you like the idea, after the learning curve and getting used to not having facial identification, it is a really fun phone."

In Berlin, YouTube content creator Patrick Wolter was impressed that the Duo works as a phone and an iPad in one.

"I've always found it a hassle to carry around a separate tablet, especially since I already have a laptop and other gear," he said. "In the long run, this will likely end up replacing those other devices."

TOUGH TO FIND

Apple's ( AAPL ) entry into the relatively niche foldables market could bring the format to a much broader audience, said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market researcher IDC.

IDC expects Apple ( AAPL ) will take 44% of the foldable market value in 2026 on 31% of units. By 2027, it will become the market leader both in value and units shipped, IDC forecast.

"Apple ( AAPL ) has made a convincing case for this form factor," Jeronimo said after spending a week with the Duo.

"Now comes the next test: turning excitement into availability, adoption and a lasting new chapter for the smartphone market," Jeronimo said.

($1 = 1.4257 Australian dollars)

($1 = 7.8410 Hong Kong dollars)

(Reporting by Aditya Soni in Bengaluru, Stephen Nellis and Nathan Frandino in San Francisco, Nicoco Chan in Shanghai, Joyce Zhou in Hong Kong, Christine Chen in Sydney, Matthias Baehr in Berlin, Will Russell and Ben Makori in London, additional reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by Will Dunham, Christopher Cushing, Kate Mayberry, Alexander Smith and Leroy Leo)

data.title: US telecom operators wobble after report SpaceX in talks for cell sites
data.description:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - US telecom stocks declined on Friday after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier, fueling concerns over fresh competition.

Elon Musk's rocket and space technology company was in talks to access at least 80,000 cell sites to build its wireless carrier from scratch, Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday, citing sources familiar with the matter.

AT&T ( T ) fell 5.6% to a more than three-month low, Verizon lost 1.6% and T-Mobile shed 5%. 

Germany's Deutsche Telekom, which holds an over 50% stake in T-Mobile, lost 3.2%.

"The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment," Bernstein analysts said in a note.

Tower operators and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The report comes weeks after SpaceX acquired low-band spectrum to advance its carrier plans, mounting a direct, orbital challenge to legacy wireless giants in the US and sending AT&T ( T ) and Verizon shares to their worst one-day falls in more than two decades.

Bernstein analysts said that an MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) deal with SpaceX may not appeal to telecom operators, but a unified stance against one has done little to lift sentiment, leaving carriers to reassess their options.

SpaceX's Starlink has been generating revenue from internet services in sparsely populated and rural areas, but becoming a true rival to major carriers will require years of work and a terrestrial network.

Tower operator Crown Castle ( CCI ), however, surged 11.6% after the report identified it as one of the cellular infrastructure companies SpaceX was in talks with. 

Other operators also rose, with American Tower ( AMT ) up 4.9% and SBA Communications ( SBAC ) adding 4.6%. 

Shares of SpaceX rose 1.7%. 

(Reporting by Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks mixed, day after AI-related selloff; oil prices rise again
data.description:
(Updates to US midday)

* Wall Street stocks mostly lower

* Oil prices extend recent gains

* US Treasury yields up; France gets respite

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Marc Jones

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.

The Nasdaq was up 0.2% after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1%.

An index of semiconductors was up about 1%. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms ( META ) reignited worries about the AI trade.

It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity."

Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.

US crude rose 2.56% to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74%. European natural gas prices jumped.

AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL

Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express ( AXP ) shares fell 3.5% after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.

Telecom company shares, including Verizon, dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9%, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 eased 11.14 points, or 0.14%, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21%, to 26,062.75.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15%, to 1,121.29. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4%.

Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4% earlier.

US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5%.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992%. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June.

EURO FALLS

The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.

French yields, which were down 5 basis points at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.

A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.

France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody's later on Friday.

The euro was last down 0.12% at $1.12, set to end the week 0.35% lower.

(Reporting by Caroline Valetkevitch in New York and Marc Jones in London; Additional reporting by Stella Qiu in Sydney; Editing by Elaine Hardcastle and Rod Nickel)

data.title: London stocks mark weekly fall as oil hits five-month high ahead of budget
data.description:
(Updates after markets close)

Oct 23 (Reuters) - Britain's FTSE 100 snapped a two-week winning streak on Friday, as oil prices at over five-month highs weighed on risk appetite, ahead of finance minister John Healey's first budget next week.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index closed 0.3% lower at 10,690.36 points. The midcap FTSE 250 ended 0.1% higher, but marked its sharpest weekly fall in six weeks.

* Energy shares advanced 3.9% as Brent crude crossed $115 a barrel

* Most sectors were lower, with aerospace and defence shares slipping 4.6% to an over five-month low

* Rolls-Royce slid 7.6%, registering its biggest one-day fall since April 2025. French rival Safran lost 10% after warning that a slowdown in aftermarket sales growth could extend into 2027

* Banks and healthcare stocks fell 0.8% and 1.1% respectively, further bogging down the index

* Data this week showed price pressures exceeded expectations in September, strengthening the case for a Bank of England interest rate hike in November, which is fully priced in

* Both the main indexes marked their first week of losses in three, as oil prices surged, bets on rate hikes grew and investors were jittery ahead of next week's budget

* Precious and industrial metal miners were among the worst performers this week, down 10.9% and 8.7% respectively

* Gold miners lost 3.7% on Friday as well, as prices of bullion fell over 1%

* British retail sales volumes fell more than expected in September, while consumer confidence slumped in October, posting its steepest monthly fall since the early stages of the pandemic, separate data showed

(Reporting by Darshan Kumar and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel and Joyjeet Das)

data.title: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Reports Survival Data for Ovarian Cancer Drug Azenosertib
data.description:
12:40 PM EDT, 10/23/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Zentalis Pharmaceuticals ( ZNTL ) on Friday presented the first overall survival results for its experimental ovarian cancer drug azenosertib.

In an interim analysis of the DENALI Part 1b study, patients whose tumors tested positive for Cyclin E1, a protein linked to aggressive cancer growth, lived a median of 15.9 months, versus 7.5 months for those who tested negative.

Among 43 evaluable Cyclin E1-positive patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, a disease that returns within six months of platinum chemotherapy, 37.2% saw tumors shrink by a predefined amount, known as objective response rate. Median duration of response was 5.5 months.

The company said the data support its ongoing DENALI Part 2 and ASPENOVA phase 3 trials.
